summary:
Authored the video-scripting and acceptance-test half of Set 106: nine files under docs/tutorials/video/ (a README, six OBS scene scripts 1:1 with the tutorial's six parts, and the Azure DevOps + direct-provider-API alternate takes) plus the 13-walk 106-hello-world-tutorial-simplification-uat-checklist.json that Session 4's live ~2-hour operator walk executes. No code: no ai_router change, no extension change, no version bump (0.46.0 from Session 2 stands, publish still operator-gated), no tag, no publish. Every beat carries Do / Say / See, cites the tutorial step it performs in a per-file traceability table, marks asynchronous waits (WAIT) and take boundaries (CUT), and adds an 'If this fails on camera' line wherever a real failure mode exists. Both alternate takes name the beats they replace, the beats they change downstream, and their rejoin point.

The routed step-3.5 analyst's risk control -- 'a full, literal desk check against a clean developer environment' -- was DECLINED with reasons and replaced: that check IS the Session 4 walk, on operator-supplied resources this session does not have, and running a half version of it would either duplicate S4 or produce partial evidence inviting S4 to be skipped. What was adopted instead is two committed, re-runnable mechanical gates (s3-check-literals.py, s3-check-checklist.py; evidence in s3-authoring-gates.md) that assert every `Dabbler: <Title>` in docs/tutorials/ resolves to a real contributed command, that 48 literals shared between the tutorial and the scripts are identical, that the CI job YAML is byte-identical between the tutorial and scene 4 AND reachable from the scaffolded template by adding steps only, that every relative link resolves, and that the checklist satisfies the ad-hoc UAT floor and the Set 078 authoring bar. Final: 107/107 and 345/345, both exit 0.

VERIFICATION IS THE STORY OF THIS SESSION. Five cross-provider rounds (openai/gpt-5-6, anthropic excluded by construction) found 18 blocking in discovery fan-out 2/2, 2 more in the supplementary completeness pass run BEFORE any remediation, then 2, then 1, then 0. After de-duplicating the fan-out that is 18 distinct defects across the loop, every one accepted and none disputed. Both gates were green while the first 15 were live -- which is exactly the limitation s3-authoring-gates.md names about itself: a correct string is not a followable instruction. The dominant class was a step that cannot be performed from the state the previous step leaves behind. Seven fixes landed in docs/tutorials/hello-world.md under the spec's scripting-exposed-gap clause and are enumerated individually in the sidecar so the judgment can be audited rather than trusted. The three that changed teaching rather than wording: CODEOWNERS already requests the reviewer once the rules are on main, so Part 6 now DEMONSTRATES routing instead of asking by hand, and the two mechanisms the old text conflated are separated (touches: authorizes cross-module work, CODEOWNERS routes review); Sam could not merge either pull request opened after approvals rose 0 -> 1, which was certain rather than an edge case; and Walk 9 required an observation `pytest -q` cannot produce, fixed by one echo line rather than by weakening the check. Two later rounds rejected fixes of this session's own making -- the privacy rule had been WEAKENED rather than satisfied (now: the ADO scratch project is public, org policy toggle scripted, hard stop if unavailable), and the Marketplace fix had swapped one unavailable dependency for another (now: do not record until the Marketplace is at 0.46.0; the local VSIX stays only in the walk, named in both places as its one deliberate departure).

THE BOUND WAS REACHED AT REMEDIATION-REVIEW CYCLE 2 AND THE SESSION STOPPED TO THE OPERATOR, who ruled: one more cycle, then a third-provider opinion, then close. Cycle 3 returned VERIFIED with zero findings and 16/16 fix verdicts accepted. THE THIRD-PROVIDER OPINION IS WHY THAT RULING MATTERED. All five rounds were judged by one provider family; the opinion went to google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview with the full 198k-char evidence bundle and the one question a same-provider re-run cannot answer -- did this converge because the work became sound, or because the verifier stopped noticing? It returned ISSUES_FOUND, convergence_assessment.genuine: false, and named a Critical five rounds had walked past: `gh auth login` writes ONE credential per OS user, and `Dabbler: Open PR for this set` runs `gh pr create`, so GitHub records a pull request's author as whoever gh is logged in as -- not whoever wrote the commits. The staging has one operator playing two people on one machine behind a second browser profile and a second clone, neither of which touches gh, so every pull request 'Sam' opens would have been authored by Priya: she could not approve them (GitHub refuses self-approval) and CODEOWNERS would never request her (it never requests an author). Walks 8 and 9 would both have dead-ended, and scene 6 beat 2 -- the payoff beat this session ADDED in round 1 -- would have shown an empty Reviewers box. Its diagnosis of the miss: the loop 'perfectly verified the logical narrative ... but completely lost sight of the physical constraints of the execution environment. It achieved 0 findings by ignoring the execution layer.' Accepted and fixed entirely in the staging -- scene 5's note, scene 5 beats 3/8/12, scene 6 beat 1, and Walks 7/8/9 now log Sam into gh as a second account and `gh auth switch` before every pull-request action, with byline checks in the See clauses and `gh auth status` pinned by the literal gate. THE TUTORIAL IS UNTOUCHED BY THIS FIX, because the tutorial is correct: real Priya and real Sam are on their own machines. It also flagged one Minor (the checklist had flattened cross-platform commands to their Windows forms), fixed with a PLATFORM paragraph in Notes. It challenged NONE of the 19 earlier fixes. That is the useful shape of the result: the document-layer loop was converging honestly, and was silent about an entire second axis it never looked at. $0.074 to learn that, against a two-hour walk that would have walled at Walk 8.

Suite green throughout on the reviewed tree: pytest 3060 passed / 6 skipped (410.82s); extension unit 1767 passing with `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Layer 3 Playwright deliberately NOT run and the reason recorded rather than assumed -- L-064-12 arms it for Explorer-rendering surfaces, state-file writers, or the fixture harness, and this session changed markdown under docs/tutorials/ plus one session-set JSON artifact. Nothing in the diff can move a pixel in the webview.

reason.specifics: THIRD consecutive routed recommendation to switch off Anthropic for this set, and the first one this session's own evidence independently argues for. The routed step-3.5 analysis (gemini-2.5-pro, anthropic excluded) named github-copilot / openai / gpt-5.6 for Session 4 -- recorded with one correction of fact, the same class as Session 1's `gpt-4o` slip: it paired the github-copilot ENGINE with gpt-5.6, which is representable (a Copilot seat's identity is its underlying model, Set 084 F1) but is not what its reasoning describes; 'a code-native OpenAI interface' is Codex, which reads AGENTS.md. engine: codex is the coherent form. The counter-argument is now at its weakest of the whole set, and this session produced the proof rather than the argument: five verification rounds on one provider family converged to VERIFIED while missing a Critical that a single $0.074 call to a THIRD family found immediately -- because the loop had settled into one axis (documents) and was blind to another (the machine). Session 4 remediates defects in documents this orchestrator family authored, found by a human walking them; an author is the worst possible reviewer of their own instructions, because they read the step they meant rather than the step they wrote. If any session of this set should change hands, it is this one. The pick remains the operator's at invocation.

residual_findings: REASONED, NOT OBSERVED (fix G). The branch-protection correction -- 'leave Require approvals unticked' rather than 'set required approvals to 0' -- comes from how GitHub's classic rule UI is structured, not from a live look at it. Checklist Walk 3's Expectation asks the operator to report whether the new wording matched the control in front of them.

REASONED, NOT OBSERVED (fix R3-2). That Organization Settings > Policies > Allow public projects exists and is toggleable by the owner of a fresh Azure DevOps organisation is reasoned. If it is not reachable, the take's own hard stop fires and Walk 11 reports that it could not run -- the designed outcome, but unobserved.

REASONED, NOT OBSERVED (fix TP-1). That the GitHub CLI supports multiple logged-in accounts and switches with `gh auth switch --user <handle>` (2.40+), and that `gh auth status` shows which is active, is reasoned from the CLI's documented surface. Walk 7 step 2 settles it one walk BEFORE the walk it protects.

UNREVIEWED FIX DELTA. The third-provider fixes (TP-1 Critical, TP-2 Minor) were applied AFTER round 5 returned VERIFIED and were not themselves put through a verifier round -- the operator's ruling was one cycle, then the opinion, then close, and reviewing this delta would have been cycle 4. They are markdown and JSON staging notes in this session's own deliverables; Session 4's walk is where they are exercised for real.

CARRIED FROM SESSION 1, STILL OWED, ROUTER-SIDE AND OUT OF SCOPE HERE: the Copilot catalog pin reconciliation. The lockfile pins CLI 1.0.69 while the operator's seat reports 1.0.75, so validate_catalog fails closed under transport.profile: copilot-cli. Set 104 S2 hand-bumped the pin without re-probing per-model entries and recorded the full --refresh as owed. Unaffected in this repo today (transport.profile: api).
PRE-EXISTING, OUT OF SCOPE (carried from Session 2): tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/package-lock.json still reads 0.41.0 while package.json is 0.46.0. Predates this set by four releases.
declined_recommendations: The routed step-3.5 analyst's single risk control -- 'the orchestrator must perform a full, literal desk check of every step in the video scripts and UAT checklist against a clean developer environment before closing the session' -- was DECLINED, and the reason is on the record because it is a judgment call. A clean-environment desk check of these scripts IS the ~2-hour Session 4 walk: it needs a GitHub account, a second account to play Sam, a Copilot seat, and a throwaway public repository, none of which this session has. Performing it here would either duplicate S4 outright or -- worse -- produce a half-walk whose partial evidence invites S4 to be skipped, which is precisely the untested-instructions gap this set exists to close. Adopted instead, cheapest first: traceability by construction (every beat cites its tutorial step, so a beat with no step is either a tutorial gap or invented ceremony); literals copied rather than paraphrased and then machine-checked byte-identical; the UAT floor machine-checked before the human is notified; and S4 left as the acceptance test it is. The verification loop then proved the declined control was pointing at something real -- 18 defects the gates could not see -- which is an argument for S4, not for a half-desk-check here.

The same analysis proposed 'add more' remedies implicitly by listing five scene-script pitfalls as advice. They were adopted as FORMAT rather than as prose: no magic transitions (every scene states the exact repo/UI state it starts from and every beat names its window), literal atomic actions, explicit WAIT beats for anything asynchronous, narration written beside rather than instead of the action, and an 'If this fails on camera' line on every beat with a known failure mode. Folding them into the structure rather than restating them keeps the set's governing verdict intact -- the teaching surface was far too large, and a fix whose remedy is 'add more' has to earn its weight.
